claim: The ventrolateral prefrontal cortex (vlPFC) mainly spans Brodmann's Areas 44, 45 a/b, 46 v/f, and 12 r/l.
source: A subdivision of the prefrontal cortex - the ventrolateral section (vlPFC), which mainly spans Brodmann's Areas 44, 45 a/b, 46 v/f, and 12 r/l (Saleem et al., 2014), is central to a variety of functions including language, objective memory, and decision-making (Sakagami and Pan, 2007; Levy and Wagner, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Saleem et al., 2014, which provides the anatomical definition of vlPFC.

claim: The vlPFC is central to a variety of functions including language, objective memory, and decision-making.
source: A subdivision of the prefrontal cortex - the ventrolateral section (vlPFC), which mainly spans Brodmann's Areas 44, 45 a/b, 46 v/f, and 12 r/l (Saleem et al., 2014), is central to a variety of functions including language, objective memory, and decision-making (Sakagami and Pan, 2007; Levy and Wagner, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Sakagami and Pan, 2007 and Levy and Wagner, 2011.

claim: Abnormalities of vlPFC are in tight association with deficits in cognitive flexibility.
source: Emerging evidence further demonstrates abnormalities of vlPFC in tight association with deficits in cognitive flexibility (Neubert et al., 2014; Cai et al., 2020; Zhan et al., 2021), suggesting that an elaborate delineation of its hard wiring would shed light on the underlying neuropathology of psychiatric disorders (Haber et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Neubert et al., 2014; Cai et al., 2020; and Zhan et al., 2021.

claim: Histological neural tracing continues to be the most reliable way of survey for all myelinated axons in mammalian brains.
source: Histological neural tracing has been historically utilized for circuit/pathway mapping and continues to be the most reliable way of survey for all myelinated axons in mammalian brains (Zeng, 2018; Luo et al., 2018; Bienkowski et al., 2018), which has also been used as a gold standard to validate other modalities like diffusion tractography (Schmahmann et al., 2007; Donahue et al., 2016; Reveley et al., 2015; Mortazavi et al., 2018; Folloni et al., 2019; Dyrby et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Zeng, 2018; Luo et al., 2018; and Bienkowski et al., 2018.

claim: Histological neural tracing has been used as a gold standard to validate diffusion tractography.
source: Histological neural tracing has been historically utilized for circuit/pathway mapping and continues to be the most reliable way of survey for all myelinated axons in mammalian brains (Zeng, 2018; Luo et al., 2018; Bienkowski et al., 2018), which has also been used as a gold standard to validate other modalities like diffusion tractography (Schmahmann et al., 2007; Donahue et al., 2016; Reveley et al., 2015; Mortazavi et al., 2018; Folloni et al., 2019; Dyrby et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Schmahmann et al., 2007; Donahue et al., 2016; Reveley et al., 2015; Mortazavi et al., 2018; Folloni et al., 2019; and Dyrby et al., 2018.

claim: Diffusion tractography represents the only methodology capable of inferring the ensemble of anatomical connections in the living animal or human brain.
source: Diffusion tractography, which has been developed in the 1990s to estimate the tissue microstructure by means of spatial encoding of water molecule movements (Basser et al., 1994), represents the only methodology capable of inferring the ensemble of anatomical connections in the living animal or human brain (Wedeen et al., 2012; Mori and Zhang, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Wedeen et al., 2012 and Mori and Zhang, 2006.

claim: Diffusion tractography is an indirect observation with limited resolution and accuracy.
source: But this technique is an indirect observation with limited resolution and accuracy, and its reliability of false negative and false positive findings remains to be fully validated in a 3D space (Donahue et al., 2016; Maier-Hein et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Donahue et al., 2016 and Maier-Hein et al., 2017.

claim: The reliability of false negative and false positive findings in diffusion tractography remains to be fully validated in a 3D space.
source: But this technique is an indirect observation with limited resolution and accuracy, and its reliability of false negative and false positive findings remains to be fully validated in a 3D space (Donahue et al., 2016; Maier-Hein et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Donahue et al., 2016 and Maier-Hein et al., 2017.

claim: Viral-based techniques for targeting specific neuronal types in macaque brain have achieved remarkable success.
source: Moreover, viral-based techniques for targeting specific neuronal types in macaque brain have achieved remarkable success (Han et al., 2009; Stauffer et al., 2016), which may furnish the requisite biological detail including excitatory and inhibitory in-/output to enrich structural network reconstructions for improved prediction of brain function (Suárez et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Han et al., 2009 and Stauffer et al., 2016.

claim: It remains unclear what type of viral vector is suitable for long-range axonal fiber tracing.
source: However, it remains unclear thus far what type of viral vector is suitable for long-range axonal fiber tracing (Zeng, 2018; Luo et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Zeng, 2018 and Luo et al., 2018.

claim: The IFOF supposedly connects the ventrolateral prefrontal cortex and medial orbitofrontal cortex to the occipital lobe through the ventral part of the external capsule.
source: The IFOF first proposed in the early 19th century supposedly connects the ventrolateral prefrontal cortex and medial orbitofrontal cortex to the occipital lobe through the ventral part of the external capsule (Curran, 1909; Catani et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Curran, 1909 and Catani et al., 2002.

claim: Micro-dissection and diffusion MRI tractography studies have confirmed the anatomy of the IFOF pathway.
source: Micro-dissection and diffusion MRI tractography studies have recently confirmed the anatomy of this pathway (Sarubbo et al., 2019; Barrett et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Sarubbo et al., 2019 and Barrett et al., 2020.

claim: A number of axonal tracing studies have failed to reveal the IFOF in the macaque brain.
source: Despite an abundance of functional evidence supporting a central role of occipito-frontal circuitry in cognition and sensory integration, a number of axonal tracing studies, which have been able to identify monosynaptic connections, have failed to reveal the IFOF in the macaque brain (Schmahmann et al., 2007; Schmahmann and Pandya, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Schmahmann et al., 2007 and Schmahmann and Pandya, 2006.

claim: Sparse connections between frontal and occipital cortices in macaques were reported by other labs.
source: By contrast, sparse connections between frontal and occipital cortices in macaques were reported by other labs (Gerbella et al., 2010; Markov et al., 2014), although they do not show whether these axons follow the course expected for the IFOF.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gerbella et al., 2010 and Markov et al., 2014.

claim: The study established a comprehensive brain-wide excitatory projectome of the vlPFC in macaque monkeys using viral-based genetic tracing in tandem with serial two-photon (STP) tomography.
source: In the present study, we aim to establish a comprehensive brain-wide excitatory projectome of the vlPFC in macaque monkeys using viral-based genetic tracing in tandem with serial two-photon (STP) tomography (Figure 1A), a technique that has successfully achieved high-throughput fluorescence imaging of the entire mouse brain by integrating two-photon microscopy and tissue sectioning (Ragan et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by the description of the study's methodology and a citation to Ragan et al., 2012.

claim: STP tomography has successfully achieved high-throughput fluorescence imaging of the entire mouse brain by integrating two-photon microscopy and tissue sectioning.
source: In the present study, we aim to establish a comprehensive brain-wide excitatory projectome of the vlPFC in macaque monkeys using viral-based genetic tracing in tandem with serial two-photon (STP) tomography (Figure 1A), a technique that has successfully achieved high-throughput fluorescence imaging of the entire mouse brain by integrating two-photon microscopy and tissue sectioning (Ragan et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Ragan et al., 2012.

claim: The study performed ex vivo dMRI scans of the entire macaque brains using an ultra-high field (11.7T) MRI scanner.
source: We also performed ex vivo dMRI scans of the entire macaque brains to track the axonal fiber tracts using an ultra-high field (11.7T) MRI scanner (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and Figure 1C showing the dMRI setup.

claim: Five days after infection with VSV-ΔG, neuronal cell bodies in the cerebral cortex and mediodorsal (MD) thalamus were clearly labeled with GFP.
source: Five days after infection with VSV-ΔG, the neuronal cell bodies in the cerebral cortex (Figure 2A and B) and mediodorsal (MD) thalamus (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) were clearly labeled with GFP, although only proximal neurites were labeled with no long-range axonal fibers detected (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 2A, B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: VSV-ΔG infection for five days resulted in only proximal neurites being labeled with no long-range axonal fibers detected.
source: Five days after infection with VSV-ΔG, the neuronal cell bodies in the cerebral cortex (Figure 2A and B) and mediodorsal (MD) thalamus (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) were clearly labeled with GFP, although only proximal neurites were labeled with no long-range axonal fibers detected (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: When VSV-ΔG infection time was extended to about a month, widespread axon loss and neuronal cell death were observed.
source: When the infection time was extended to about a month, we observed widespread axon loss and neuronal cell death (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D-G).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1D-G.

claim: Long-term-infected neurons with VSV-ΔG underwent morphological changes such as membrane blebbing, a key morphological change associated with the induction of apoptosis.
source: The long-term-infected neurons underwent morphological changes such as membrane blebbing (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C), a key morphological change associated with the induction of apoptosis.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description, reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C, and established knowledge about membrane blebbing.

claim: Local injection with VSV-ΔG mediated rapid and transient gene expression nearby the injection site.
source: Local injection with VSV-ΔG mediated rapid and transient gene expression nearby the injection site, and an extension of infection time evidently caused fatal neurotoxicity.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental observations described in the text.

claim: An extension of VSV-ΔG infection time evidently caused fatal neurotoxicity.
source: Local injection with VSV-ΔG mediated rapid and transient gene expression nearby the injection site, and an extension of infection time evidently caused fatal neurotoxicity.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental observations described in the text.

claim: Lenti-Ubic-GFP exhibited stable expression in the cell soma even after 9 months.
source: Lenti-Ubic-GFP exhibited stable expression in the cell soma even after 9 months (Figure 2C and D), despite sparse labeling of GFP positive axons (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 2C and D.

claim: Lenti-Ubic-GFP resulted in sparse labeling of GFP positive axons.
source: Lenti-Ubic-GFP exhibited stable expression in the cell soma even after 9 months (Figure 2C and D), despite sparse labeling of GFP positive axons (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Six weeks after AAV2/9-CaMKIIa-Tau-GFP was injected into the premotor cortex or MD thalamus, axonal fiber bundles like anterior limb of internal capsule (ALIC) were clearly visualized over several centimeters.
source: By contrast, 6 weeks after AAV2/9-CaMKIIa-Tau-GFP was injected into the premotor cortex (Figure 2E-G) or MD thalamus (Figure 2—figure supplement 4), axonal fiber bundles like anterior limb of internal capsule (ALIC) (Figure 2G) were clearly visualized over several centimeters.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 2E-G, Figure 2—figure supplement 4, and Figure 2G.

claim: AAV-infected cells were positive for the neuronal specific marker NeuN, but negative for astrocyte specific marker GFAP.
source: The AAV-infected cells were positive for the neuronal specific marker NeuN, but negative for astrocyte specific marker GFAP (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: The signal intensity of most Tau-GFP labeled axons was consistently higher than that of mCherry labeled axons.
source: As a validation test, AAV2/9 construct encoding mCherry was co-injected with AAV2/9 construct encoding Tau-GFP into the premotor cortex. And we found that the signal intensity of most Tau-GFP labeled axons was consistently higher than that of mCherry labeled axons (Figure 2—figure supplement 6A-D).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 6A-D.

claim: The density of axonal fibers labeled by AAV2/9 was significantly higher than by Lentivirus and VSV-ΔG.
source: The density of axonal fibers labeled by AAV2/9 (Figure 2—figure supplement 7C) was significantly higher (P < 0.001, Figure 2—figure supplement 7D) than by Lentivirus (Figure 2—figure supplement 7B) and VSV-ΔG (Figure 2—figure supplement 7A).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description, statistical analysis (P < 0.001), and references to Figure 2—figure supplement 7A-D.

claim: Axons labeled by lentivirus were significantly denser than by VSV-ΔG distant from the injection site.
source: Axons labeled by lentivirus (Figure 2—figure supplement 7B) were also significantly denser (P < 0.01, Figure 2—figure supplement 7D) than by VSV-ΔG (Figure 2—figure supplement 7A) distant from the injection site.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description, statistical analysis (P < 0.01), and references to Figure 2—figure supplement 7A, B, and D.

claim: AAV2/9 encoding Tau-GFP under the control of excitatory promoter CaMKIIa was determined as an anterograde tracer for mapping the excitatory projectome of vlPFC.
source: AAV2/9 encoding Tau-GFP under the control of excitatory promoter CaMKIIa was determined as an anterograde tracer for mapping the excitatory projectome of vlPFC.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental design and methodology described in the text.

claim: The injection site in vlPFC, including area 45, 12 l, and 44, was precisely located in cortical gray matter.
source: The injection site in vlPFC, validated by STP images, including area 45, 12 l, and 44, was precisely located in cortical gray matter (Figure 4A-D).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 4A-D.

claim: GFP-positive neurons in the injection site were observed positive for CaMkIIa and negative for GABA, indicating that the AAV labeled neurons were glutamate excitatory neurons.
source: To identify the cell type specificity of Tau-GFP gene expression driven by the CaMKII-α promoter, immunofluorescent staining was performed with antibodies against the excitatory neuron specific marker CaMKII-α and the inhibitory neuron-specific neurotransmitter GABA. GFP-positive neurons in the injection site were observed positive for CaMkIIa (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-C) and negative for GABA (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D-F), indicating that the AAV labeled neurons were glutamate excitatory neurons.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-F.

claim: GFP-labeled projecting axons from vlPFC largely encompassed the anterior part of the brain including the frontal lobe, temporal lobe, limbic regions, insular, and some subcortical regions, but no labeled axons were found in the occipital lobe.
source: The GFP-labeled projecting axons largely encompassed the anterior part of the brain including the frontal lobe, temporal lobe, limbic regions, insular, and some subcortical regions, but no labeled axons were found in the occipital lobe (Figure 3A–C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 3A–C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Within the frontal lobe, GFP-labeled projecting axons were markedly dense in the OFC, rostrally distributed in area 12 m, 12o, 11 l, 13 l, and 13 m.
source: Within the frontal lobe, GFP-labeled projecting axons were markedly dense in the OFC, rostrally distributed in area 12 m (Figure 4E, F and G), 12o (Figure 4E), 11 l (Figure 4E, H and I), 13 l (Figure 4E), and 13 m (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 4E-I.

claim: The 12 m received strongest innervation from vlPFC relative to other OFC subregions.
source: The 12 m received strongest innervation from vlPFC relative to other OFC subregions (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 4E.

claim: Axonal projections from vlPFC were found in the FEF including 8Av and 8Ad.
source: Laterally, axonal projections were found in the FEF including 8Av (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A, B and C) and 8Ad (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 4—figure supplement 2A-D.

claim: Dense axonal fibers from vlPFC were found in the dorsal prefrontal cortex, including area 8Bd, 8Bm, 8Bs, 46d, and 9d.
source: Dorsally, there were dense axonal fibers in the dorsal prefrontal cortex, including area 8Bd (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E, F and G), 8Bm (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E), 8Bs (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E), 46d (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E, H and I), and 9d (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E, J and K).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 4—figure supplement 2E-K.

claim: The 8Bd and 46d received relatively more innervation from vlPFC compared with 9d, 8Bs, and 8Bm.
source: The 8Bd and 46d received relatively more innervation compared with 9d, 8Bs, and 8Bm (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Scattered axon fibers from vlPFC were visible in area F5, F7, and F2 of the premotor cortex.
source: On the medial surface of the brain, scattered axon fibers were visible in area F5 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2L and M), F7 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2L and N), and F2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2L) of the premotor cortex.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 4—figure supplement 2L-N.

claim: The axons from vlPFC within the premotor cortex exhibited a gradient pattern with the largest axon distribution along the anterior part.
source: The axons with the premotor cortex exhibited a gradient pattern with the largest axon distribution along the anterior part (Figure 4—figure supplement 2L).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 2L.

claim: Axons from vlPFC were noted in the precentral opercular area (PrCO) and medial prefrontal area (mainly in 10mr).
source: In addition, axons were noted in the precentral opercular area (PrCO) and medial prefrontal area (mainly in 10mr) (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3C.

claim: The projections from vlPFC anchored in the prefrontal cortex formed isolated clusters.
source: Interestingly, the projections anchored in the prefrontal cortex of these axonal fibers formed isolated clusters (Figure 4F and H, indicated by arrows).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 4F and H.

claim: The z-axis extent of axonal clusters from vlPFC was ranging from 1.2 mm to 3.8 mm (2.24 ± 0.80 mm).
source: The z-axis extent of axonal clusters was ranging from 1.2 mm to 3.8 mm (2.24 ± 0.80 mm) (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description, quantitative measurements, and reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Rich connections from vlPFC were observed in the temporal lobe, predominantly in caudal lateral (CL), caudal (CPB), and rostral (RPB) portions of parabelt region of the auditory cortex.
source: Beyond the frontal lobe, rich connections were observed in the temporal lobe (Figure 3), predominantly in caudal lateral (CL), caudal (CPB), and rostral (RPB) portions of parabelt region of the auditory cortex; anterior TE (TEa), medial TE (TEm), superior temporal polysensory area (STP, correspond to areas PGa and TPO), IPa and TAa of the dorsal bank/ventral bank/fundus of the superior temporal sulcus (STSd/v/f) (Figure 3C); medial superior temporal area (MST), floor of superior temporal area (FST), anteroventral TE (TEav), anterodorsal TE (TEad), and area TEO of superior temporal area.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 3 and Figure 3C.

claim: The vlPFC sends axons to limbic regions, mainly in 24 a, 24 a', 24b, 24b', and 24 c of anterior cingulate areas (ACC).
source: The vlPFC also sends axons to limbic regions, mainly in 24 a, 24 a', 24b, 24b',and 24 c of anterior cingulate areas (ACC) (Figure 3C); area TF of parahippocampal cortex (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3C.

claim: Relatively weak projections from vlPFC were observed in the dorsal subdivision of lateral intraparietal area (LIPd); 7 a and 7b of inferior parietal lobule areas; secondary somatosensory area (SII) and parietal operculum (7op) of the parietal cortex.
source: Relatively weak projections were observed in the dorsal subdivision of lateral intraparietal area (LIPd); 7 a and 7b of inferior parietal lobule areas; secondary somatosensory area (SII) and parietal operculum (7op) of the parietal cortex (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3C.

claim: Sparsely labeled axons from vlPFC were found in the granular insula (Ig) and lateral agranular insula (Ial) area.
source: There were some sparsely labeled axons in the granular insula (Ig) and lateral agranular insula (Ial) area (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3C.

claim: Traveling axonal bundles from vlPFC were found in the corpus callosum, anterior limb of internal capsule (ALIC), and anchored into the MD thalamus.
source: In white matter, traveling axonal bundles were found in the corpus callosum, anterior limb of internal capsule (ALIC, Figure 4—figure supplement 4A, B), and anchored into the MD thalamus (Figure 4—figure supplement 4C, D).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 4—figure supplement 4A-D.

claim: Axon clusters from vlPFC were observed in the medial and caudal parts of caudate.
source: Subcortically, axon clusters were observed in the medial (Figure 4—figure supplement 4F, G) and caudal (Figure 4—figure supplement 4H) parts of caudate.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 4—figure supplement 4F-H.

claim: Axons in MD and caudate from vlPFC were thinner than those in the ALIC.
source: High resolution confocal images revealed that axons in MD (Figure 4—figure supplement 4D) and caudate (Figure 4—figure supplement 4J) were thinner than those in the ALIC (Figure 4—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 4—figure supplement 4B, D, and J.

claim: Labeled axons from vlPFC were found extending to the parvicellular part of accessory basal nucleus of amygdala (ABpc), reticulate and compacta parts of substantia nigra (SNr/c), claustrum and subthalamic nucleus (STN).
source: Furthermore, the labeled axons were found extending to the parvicellular part of accessory basal nucleus of amygdala (ABpc), reticulate and compacta parts of substantia nigra (SNr/c), claustrum and subthalamic nucleus (STN) (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 3C.

claim: The Dice coefficients and Pearson coefficients between GFP projection and probabilistic tract were higher in dense projection regions, especially for the vlPFC-CC-contralateral tract.
source: GFP projection and probabilistic tract were plotted with the Dice coefficients and Pearson coefficients (R) along the anterior-posterior axis of the whole macaque brain. The Dice coefficients and Pearson coefficients were higher in dense projection regions, especially for the vlPFC-CC-contralateral tract (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 6A.

claim: The dMRI-derived tracts largely overlapped with the axonal bundles shown in STP images for the vlPFC-CC-contralateral tract.
source: Upon visual comparison, the dMRI-derived tracts largely overlapped with the axonal bundles shown in STP images (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 6B and C.

claim: For all slices along vlPFC-CC-contralateral tract, consistent and significant correlations were observed between STP and dMRI modalities (R = 0.4624 ± 0.0922; Dice = 0.4312 ± 0.0861).
source: For all slices (spaced by 500 μm) along vlPFC-CC-contralateral tract, we observed consistent and significant correlations between these two modalities (R = 0.4624 ± 0.0922; Dice = 0.4312 ± 0.0861).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and quantitative statistical measures.

claim: The inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus (IFOF) in macaques is a long-ranged bowtie-shaped tract as illustrated by diffusion tractography.
source: As illustrated by diffusion tractography, the inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus (IFOF) in macaques is a long-ranged bowtie-shaped tract (Figure 7A), showing traveling course similar to humans.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 7A.

claim: The frontal stem of IFOF spread to form a thin sheet, and its temporal stem narrowed in coronal section, mainly gathered at the external capsule.
source: The frontal stem of IFOF spread to form a thin sheet, and its temporal stem narrowed in coronal section, mainly gathered at the external capsule.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description of the IFOF anatomy.

claim: The posterior part of vlPFC axonal projections apparently ends at the middle superior temporal region, far from the occipital lobe.
source: The intersection between IFOF and axonal projections of vlPFC was shown in a common 3D space of diffusion tractography in Figure 7B, whereby the posterior part of vlPFC axonal projections apparently ends at the middle superior temporal region, far from the occipital lobe.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 7B.

claim: The Szymkiewicz-Simpson overlap coefficient between the IFOF tract and vlPFC projectome was 0.0397 and 0.0535 in 3D space for two dMRI data sets, indicating that only a small fraction of the IFOF tract and vlPFC projectome overlapped.
source: To quantify the spatial correspondence between the IFOF tract and vlPFC projectome, the Szymkiewicz-Simpson overlap coefficient was calculated in a shared common 3D space after co-registration. It was 0.0397 and 0.0535 in 3D space for two dMRI data sets, indicating that only a small fraction of the IFOF tract and vlPFC projectome overlapped (mainly in the front half of the brain, Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description, quantitative measurements, and reference to Figure 7.

claim: The anterior part of the vlPFC axonal projections shown by STP tomography largely overlapped with the dMRI-derived IFOF tracts in frontal whiter matter, external capsule, claustrum, and extreme capsule.
source: The anterior part of the vlPFC axonal projections shown by STP tomography largely overlapped with the dMRI-derived IFOF tracts in frontal whiter matter (Figure 7D), external capsule (Figure 7E), claustrum (Figure 7E and F), and extreme capsule (Figure 7F).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and references to Figure 7D-F.

claim: The posterior part of dMRI-derived IFOF tract passed through temporal white matter, whereas the posterior part of fiber projections of vlPFC sent no axons to this region.
source: Meanwhile, the posterior part of dMRI-derived IFOF tract passed through temporal white matter (Figure 7G), whereas the posterior part of fiber projections of vlPFC sent no axons to this region (Figure 7G).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 7G.

claim: The dMRI-derived SLFIII substantially overlapped with the vlPFC axonal projections in frontal and parietal whiter matter along the whole trajectory.
source: Unlike the IFOF in which the results of diffusion tractography mainly overlapped with those of viral tracing in the anterior part (Figure 7), the dMRI-derived SLFIII substantially overlapped with the vlPFC axonal projections in frontal and parietal whiter matter along the whole trajectory (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Szymkiewicz-Simpson overlap coefficients between the SLFIII derived from diffusion tractography and the parietal branch of vlPFC projections identified from viral tracing showed markedly high overlap (r = 0.2603 and 0.2175).
source: Similarly, we calculated the Szymkiewicz-Simpson overlap coefficients between the SLFIII derived from diffusion tractography and the parietal branch of vlPFC projections identified from viral tracing in two brain samples, as showed markedly high overlap (r = 0.2603 and 0.2175).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and quantitative measurements.

claim: STP tomography was customized for whole-brain imaging of the macaque monkey at submicron resolution.
source: We customized STP tomography for whole-brain imaging of the macaque monkey at submicron resolution and accomplished brain-wide 3D reconstruction of axonal connectome, thanks to prominent characteristics of STP tomography including free of tissue distortions, no need for section-to-section alignment, and high-resolution image sets readily warped in 3D space (Amato et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and a citation to Amato et al., 2016.

claim: STP tomography has prominent characteristics including free of tissue distortions, no need for section-to-section alignment, and high-resolution image sets readily warped in 3D space.
source: We customized STP tomography for whole-brain imaging of the macaque monkey at submicron resolution and accomplished brain-wide 3D reconstruction of axonal connectome, thanks to prominent characteristics of STP tomography including free of tissue distortions, no need for section-to-section alignment, and high-resolution image sets readily warped in 3D space (Amato et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and a citation to Amato et al., 2016.

claim: A CaMKIIα promoter carried by lentivirus was able to target excitatory neurons with optogenetic proteins in the macaque brain.
source: Previous studies have demonstrated that a CaMKIIα promoter carried by lentivirus was able to target excitatory neurons with optogenetic proteins in the macaque brain (Han et al., 2009), and a TH promoter carried by AAV selectively targeted dopamine neurons (Stauffer et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Han et al., 2009.

claim: A TH promoter carried by AAV selectively targeted dopamine neurons.
source: Previous studies have demonstrated that a CaMKIIα promoter carried by lentivirus was able to target excitatory neurons with optogenetic proteins in the macaque brain (Han et al., 2009), and a TH promoter carried by AAV selectively targeted dopamine neurons (Stauffer et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Stauffer et al., 2016.

claim: Immunofluorescent staining with both CaMKIIα and GABA confirmed that GFP was specifically expressed in excitatory neurons.
source: Here we deployed AAV with CaMKIIα promoter to focus on the excitatory projection of vlPFC, whereby immunofluorescent staining with both CaMKIIα and GABA confirmed that GFP was specifically expressed in excitatory neurons.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description of the experimental validation.

claim: The excitatory projection of vlPFC to the rest of brain was compatible with previous reports using chemical tracers.
source: We found the excitatory projection of vlPFC to the rest of brain was compatible with previous reports using chemical tracers (Borra et al., 2011; Gerbella et al., 2010; Safadi et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Borra et al., 2011; Gerbella et al., 2010; and Safadi et al., 2018.

claim: The vlPFC connectivity profile shown in this study was markedly similar to that of CoCoMac.
source: Furthermore, we compared the current vlPFC projectome data with the well-known macaque connectivity database CoCoMac (Bakker et al., 2012), which includes the results of several hundred published axonal tract-tracing studies in the macaque monkey brain (Stephan, 2013). Essentially the vlPFC connectivity profile shown here was markedly similar to that of CoCoMac, except that vlPFC projections to PFCol, PFCdm, PFCdl, PFCoi, PFCm, PMCvl, amygdala, and SII have not been reported in CoCoMac database or reported merely with unspecified strength.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and citations to Bakker et al., 2012 and Stephan, 2013.

claim: There was high correspondence between synaptic EGFP and cytoplasmic EGFP signals in target regions.
source: One recent study compared results of terminal labeling using Synaptophysin-EGFP-expressing AAV (specifically labeling synaptic endings) with the cytoplasmic EGFP AAV (labeling axon fibers and synaptic endings). There was high correspondence between synaptic EGFP and cytoplasmic EGFP signals in target regions (Oh et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Oh et al., 2014.

claim: VSV was initially utilized as a transsynaptic tracer because VSV encodes five genes, including G protein which promotes anterograde transsynaptic spread among neurons.
source: VSV was initially utilized as a transsynaptic tracer in a previous study since VSV encodes five genes, including G protein which promotes anterograde transsynaptic spread among neurons (Beier et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Beier et al., 2011.

claim: VSV-G failed to label transsynaptic cells at distant areas.
source: But we found that a shorter expression time of VSV-ΔG was insufficient to label axons traveling long distance whereas a longer expression time of VSV-ΔG caused cell death, consistent with a prior finding that VSV-G failed to label transsynaptic cells at distant areas (Mundell et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Mundell et al., 2015.

claim: Lentivirus is derived from human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1).
source: The advantage of lentivirus, which is derived from human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) (Naldini et al., 1996), is that it has a large genetic capacity of approximately 10 Kb which allows for the expression of multiple gene and usage of more than one promoter or regulatory elements.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Naldini et al., 1996.

claim: Lentivirus has a large genetic capacity of approximately 10 Kb which allows for the expression of multiple gene and usage of more than one promoter or regulatory elements.
source: The advantage of lentivirus, which is derived from human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) (Naldini et al., 1996), is that it has a large genetic capacity of approximately 10 Kb which allows for the expression of multiple gene and usage of more than one promoter or regulatory elements.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and established knowledge about lentivirus.

claim: AAV has minimal toxicity, weak host immune response, and stable gene expression in neurons with extraordinarily high transfection efficiency.
source: As an effective carrier for gene delivery into the brain, AAV has a number of established advantages including minimal toxicity, weak host immune response, stable gene expression in neurons with extraordinarily high transfection efficiency (titers up to 1012–1013 genome copies per mL) (Bedbrook et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Bedbrook et al., 2018.

claim: AAVs usually deliver gene cassettes of approximately 4.8 Kb.
source: One major drawback of AAV vectors is the limited packaging capacity. AAVs usually deliver gene cassettes of approximately 4.8 Kb (i.e. one or two small genes) (Nassi et al., 2015), which has motivated us in pursuit of biocompatible nano-based carriers (Cui et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Nassi et al., 2015.

claim: Different AAV serotypes have distinct transfection bases toward various cell types in the brain.
source: It is well known that different AAV serotypes have their own sequences in the inverted terminal repeats such that they have distinct transfection bases toward various cell types in the brain.
evidence: The claim is supported by established knowledge about AAV serotypes.

claim: AAV2 is the most widely used AAV vector and effectively transfects neurons of nonhuman primates.
source: Previous studies have shown that AAV2 is the most widely used AAV vector and effectively transfects neurons of nonhuman primates (Watakabe et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Watakabe et al., 2015.

claim: AAV and BDA showed long-range projections with similar patterns when co-injected into one brain region in a mouse model, except that BDA had more retrograde-labeled neurons, probably uptaken by passing fibers in some areas.
source: In a recent report on a mouse model, researchers co-injected AAV and a classical antegrade tracer - biotinylated dextran amine (BDA) into one brain region and observed long-range projections with similar patterns by both tracers, except that BDA had more retrograde-labeled neurons, probably uptaken by passing fibers in some areas (Oh et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Oh et al., 2014.

claim: AAV2/9 vector was more suitable for long-range axonal fiber tracing, while VSV-ΔG was suitable for rapid gene expression and lentivirus for long-term gene expression in macaques.
source: Together, our results have demonstrated that AAV2/9 vector was more suitable for long-range axonal fiber tracing, while VSV-ΔG was suitable for rapid gene expression and lentivirus for long-term gene expression in macaques.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental results described in the text.

claim: Pioneering studies on cross-modality comparison across the whole-brain scale have been done by constructing a connectivity matrix using dMRI-based tractography and tracer-injection tracing in mice and in monkeys.
source: Pioneering studies on cross-modality comparison across the whole-brain scale have been done by constructing a connectivity matrix using dMRI-based tractography and tracer-injection tracing in mice (Calabrese et al., 2015) and in monkeys (Donahue et al., 2016; Girard et al., 2020; van den Heuvel et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Calabrese et al., 2015; Donahue et al., 2016; Girard et al., 2020; and van den Heuvel et al., 2015.

claim: The spatial correspondence of axonal fibers derived from diffusion tractography and GFP-labeled fluorescent images have been compared both in mice and in macaques.
source: The spatial correspondence of axonal fibers derived from diffusion tractography and GFP-labeled fluorescent images have been compared both in mice (Harsan et al., 2013; Chen et al., 2015; Chang et al., 2017) and in macaques (Dauguet et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Harsan et al., 2013; Chen et al., 2015; Chang et al., 2017; and Dauguet et al., 2007.

claim: The somatosensory and motor tracts derived from diffusion tractography were visually in good agreement with the reconstructed 3D histological sections labeled by anterograde WGA-HRP tracer in a monkey brain.
source: Dauguet and coworkers found that the somatosensory and motor tracts derived from diffusion tractography were visually in good agreement with the reconstructed 3D histological sections labeled by anterograde WGA-HRP tracer in a monkey brain, but suffered certain limitations for regions at remote locations from seeds (Dauguet et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Dauguet et al., 2007.

claim: Structural connectivity analyses based on histological datasets provided varying correlative evidence between diffusion tractography and tracer data (like r = 0.21 and r = 0.59).
source: Moreover, the structural connectivity analyses based on the histological dataset provided varying correlative evidence between these two measurements (like r = 0.21 van den Heuvel et al., 2015 using the CoCoMac tracer data Stephan, 2013 and r = 0.59 Donahue et al., 2016 using the tracer connectivity matrix from Markov et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to van den Heuvel et al., 2015; Stephan, 2013; Donahue et al., 2016; and Markov et al., 2014.

claim: GFP-labeled axonal density maps significantly overlapped with dMRI-derived probabilistic maps throughout the traveling course and demonstrated comparable connectivity strengths and patterns.
source: We observed that GFP-labeled axonal density maps not only significantly overlapped with dMRI-derived probabilistic maps throughout the traveling course but also demonstrated comparable connectivity strengths and patterns.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental results described in the text.

claim: Diffusion tractography estimated the Brownian motion of water molecules, from which the directionality of axons cannot be distinguished.
source: But caution should be born in mind that diffusion tractography estimated the Brownian motion of water molecules, from which the directionality of axons cannot be distinguished (Mori and Zhang, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Mori and Zhang, 2006.

claim: The viral tracing data contained only anterograde axonal fiber projections.
source: The viral tracing data here contained only anterograde axonal fiber projections.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description of the experimental design.

claim: The anatomy of the IFOF pathway in human has been shown by micro-dissection and diffusion tractography studies.
source: The IFOF in human brain was first described in the early 20th century (Curran, 1909), whereby the anatomy of this pathway in human has been recently shown by micro-dissection and diffusion tractography studies (Hau et al., 2016; Takemura et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hau et al., 2016 and Takemura et al., 2017.

claim: The IFOF's entire course through the ventral part of the external capsule connects the occipital cortex and the parietal and temporal cortices to the frontal cortex.
source: Its entire course through the ventral part of the external capsule (EC) connects the occipital cortex and the parietal and temporal cortices to the frontal cortex (Sarubbo et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sarubbo et al., 2019.

claim: Some axonal tracing studies showed connections between frontal and occipital lobes in monkeys.
source: Some axonal tracing studies showed connections between frontal and occipital lobes in monkeys (Gerbella et al., 2010; Markov et al., 2014), which was consistent with the observation by tractography (Feng et al., 2017) and blunt dissection (Sarubbo et al., 2019) experiments.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gerbella et al., 2010 and Markov et al., 2014.

claim: Ex-vivo tractography showed fiber connections between frontal and occipital lobes in monkeys, matching the trajectory of IFOF in humans.
source: Using the same ROIs seeds as prior studies (Barrett et al., 2020; Feng et al., 2017), our ex-vivo tractography did show fiber connections between frontal and occipital lobes in monkeys, matching the trajectory of IFOF in humans.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and citations to Barrett et al., 2020 and Feng et al., 2017.

claim: Using anterograde AAV vector without trans-synaptic capability, vlPFC fiber projections passed through external capsule, claustrum, and extreme capsule and anchored to the middle superior temporal region, but never reached the occipital lobe.
source: By contrast, using anterograde AAV vector without trans-synaptic capability, we found that vlPFC fiber projections passed through external capsule, claustrum, and extreme capsule and anchored to the middle superior temporal region. Although the trajectory of vlPFC between frontal and temporal regions matched well with the diffusion tractography of IFOF, axonal projections of vlPFC never reached the occipital lobe.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental results described in the text.

claim: Direct monosynaptic connections were reported between subdivisions of PFC such as OFC and the visual cortex in mice.
source: Nevertheless, unlike the direct monosynaptic connections reported between subdivisions of PFC such as OFC and the visual cortex in mice (Zingg et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2020), our results underscore a nontrivial species difference and raise interesting questions about the long-range brain organization and the functional role of superior temporal area in primates which definitely merits future examination.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Zingg et al., 2014 and Liu et al., 2020.

claim: The study presents a detailed excitatory connectivity projection map from vlPFC to the entire macaque brain.
source: In summary, we present a detailed excitatory connectivity projection map from vlPFC to the entire macaque brain, and demonstrate a broadly applicable roadmap of integrating 3D STP tomography labeled with antero-/retro-grade tracer and diffusion tractography for the mesoscopic mapping of brain circuits in the primate species.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description of the study's findings.

claim: The study demonstrates a broadly applicable roadmap of integrating 3D STP tomography labeled with antero-/retro-grade tracer and diffusion tractography for the mesoscopic mapping of brain circuits in the primate species.
source: In summary, we present a detailed excitatory connectivity projection map from vlPFC to the entire macaque brain, and demonstrate a broadly applicable roadmap of integrating 3D STP tomography labeled with antero-/retro-grade tracer and diffusion tractography for the mesoscopic mapping of brain circuits in the primate species.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description of the study's methodological contribution.

claim: Ten adult macaque monkeys (Macaca mulatta and Macaca fascicularis) weighting 3.5–12.2 kg (6.94 ± 2.98 kg) were used in this study from November 2015 till November 2020.
source: From November 2015 till November 2020, ten adult macaque monkeys (Macaca mulatta and Macaca fascicularis) weighting 3.5–12.2 kg (6.94 ± 2.98 kg) were used for in this study (Table 1), two of which (Macaca fascicularis) were used for ex-vivo ultrahigh field dMRI scanning.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description of the study subjects.

claim: All experimental procedures for nonhuman primate research in this study were approved by the Animal Care Committee of Shanghai Institutes for Biological Sciences, Chinese Academy of Sciences, and conformed to the National Institutes of Health guidelines for the humane care and use of laboratory animals.
source: All experimental procedures for nonhuman primate research in this study were approved by the Animal Care Committee of Shanghai Institutes for Biological Sciences, Chinese Academy of Sciences, and conformed to the National Institutes of Health guidelines for the humane care and use of laboratory animals.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description of ethical approval.

claim: The STP tomography system was integrated with a two-photon microscope and a vibratome, both of which were computer controlled and fully automated.
source: Fluorescence signals of AAV labeled areas were detected and recorded using a customized STP tomography (Figure 1—figure supplement 1). To image the monkey brain, we customized the STP tomography system which was integrated a two-photon microscope (Bruker) with a vibratome (WPI) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), computer controlled and fully automated.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The traveling range of XYZ stage was customized to 50 by 60 by 70 mm to cover the entire macaque brain.
source: The XY stage covered a 50*60 mm2 area, and the 3D scanning of Z-volume stacks was achieved with using a stepper motor (Thorlabs) that traveled over 70 mm.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description of the STP system specifications.

claim: High x-y resolution (0.95 μm/pixel) serial 2D images were acquired in the coronal plane at a z-interval of 200 μm across the entire macaque brain.
source: High x-y resolution (0.95 μm/pixel) serial 2D images were acquired in the coronal plane at a z-interval of 200 μm across the entire macaque brain.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description of the imaging parameters.

claim: The scanning time of a single field-of-view which contains 1,024 by 1,024 pixels was 1.629 s, resulting in a continuous ~1 month scanning and ~5 TB STP tomography data for a single monkey brain.
source: The scanning time of a single field-of-view which contains 1,024 by 1,024 pixels was 1.629 s (i.e. pixel residence time was ~1.6 μs), as resulted in a continuous ~1 month scanning and ~5 TB STP tomography data for a single monkey brain (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: A machine learning algorithm was adopted to reliably segment the GFP labeled axonal fibers including axonal varicosities, and remove the lipofuscin background.
source: During quantitative analysis, a machine learning algorithm was adopted to reliably segment the GFP labeled axonal fibers including axonal varicosities, and remove the lipofuscin background (Arganda-Carreras et al., 2017; Gehrlach et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and citations to Arganda-Carreras et al., 2017 and Gehrlach et al., 2020.

claim: The total computational time for the machine learning predictions in one macaque brain was ~1.5 months.
source: The total computational time for the machine learning predictions in one macaque brain was ~1.5 months.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description of the computational requirements.

claim: The precision–recall F measure (F-score) for the classifier performance was 94.41 ± 1.99%.
source: To evaluate overall classifier performance, the precision–recall F measure, also called F-score, was computed by using additional four labeled images as test sets. Higher accuracy performance achieved by the classifier often yield higher F-scores (94.41 ± 1.99%, mean ± S.E.M.).
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and quantitative measurements.

claim: Typical SNRs of diffusion images with b = 0 and b = 4000 in the present study were 48.34 ± 8.50 and 23.13 ± 2.05, respectively.
source: Typical SNRs of diffusion images with b = 0 and b = 4000 in the present study were 48.34 ± 8.50 and 23.13 ± 2.05, respectively.
evidence: The claim is supported by the text description and quantitative measurements.

claim: The SNR of b = 0 s/mm2 images should be minimally larger than 20 for obtaining relatively unbiased measures of parameters such as FA.
source: As a rule of thumb, the SNR of b = 0 s/mm2 images should be minimally larger than 20 for obtaining relatively unbiased measures of parameters such as FA (Mukherjee et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Mukherjee et al., 2008.
